name: Reeded Glass
description: The product stands in front of a sheet of real reeded cast glass, and the two flat painted panels behind it are chopped by the flutes into hard vertical color bands whose straight seam staggers in discrete offset steps — because every half-cylinder flute is a genuine cylindrical lens, not a filter.
lighting: Grazing crest speculars, unlit backdrop panels
subject: product
prompt: the subject standing 20cm in front of a full-height sheet of 20mm-pitch reeded cast glass with vertical ribs, two flat matte-painted panels 40cm behind the glass — cadmium orange on the left, ultramarine blue on the right — chopped by the flutes into hard vertical color bands whose straight seam staggers in discrete offset steps flute to flute rather than curving, a faint green iron tint and scattered seed bubbles visible in the glass edges, frosted ground edges seated in a brushed-aluminium foot channel, one bare head raking almost flat across the glass face so every flute crest picks up a single thin hard white specular line running its full height, a soft parabolic key at camera-right throwing one honest contact shadow across a matte chalk-white base, flat painted panels with no gradients, the scene filling the frame edge to edge with no border or letterbox, immaculate commercial-render clarity
